one_sentence_story: In 1992 in Parma, Giacomo Rizzolatti's team heard a 'motor' neuron crackle over a loudspeaker while the observer sat completely still watching someone else pick up a raisin — revealing how premotor circuits map watched goal-directed actions onto your own motor repertoire.
so_what_for_you: Use your premotor simulation system for real skill learning — alternate watching slow close-up hand mechanics with immediate physical reps — while skipping 2000s pop-hype claiming one cell type explains all human empathy.

jargon_map.plain: visuomotor cells in ventral premotor (F5) and inferior parietal cortex that fire both when executing a goal-directed action and when observing someone else perform that goal
jargon_map.analogy: like a piano key vibrating sympathetically when someone sings that exact note across the room

jargon_map.plain: mirror cells firing for reaching to grasp a real object (even behind a screen) while ignoring empty-air pantomime
jargon_map.analogy: like caring about catching a ball rather than waving an empty glove

jargon_map.plain: Heyes's finding that wiring sight to motor cells strengthens whenever we repeatedly watch our own hands act
jargon_map.analogy: like pairing sheet music notes with finger positions through practice

jargon_map.plain: Hickok's distinction showing premotor resonance aids motor prediction/imitation while conceptual understanding survives frontal damage
jargon_map.analogy: like a subtitle track helping you follow a film without being the projector itself
